summary: Kay Koppedrayer specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed a BA at McGill University and an MA at McMaster University, and she is a retired faculty member of Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2005).

Kazi Dawa Samdup (1868–1922) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu, he served as headmaster there (~1906–1919) and became a lecturer at the University of Calcutta in 1920.

Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992), lectured at the University of Miyazaki (~1953–1968), and was a professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1968–1995).

Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. After earning his degrees at Waseda University, he taught at Tokushima University and the National Institute of Japanese Literature before serving at Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Soichi Nakamura, served as scholar-in-residence at the San Francisco Zen Center from 1977 to 1984, and became a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He spent his career at Shuchiin University, where he served as associate professor (attested 1982–1990) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013).

Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) is a geographer and Tibetologist. He earned degrees from Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc), and became a geography professor in the Graduate School of Letters at Kyoto University around 1999.

Kazuhiko Atsumi (1928–2019) worked in philosophy and related fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954), where he later held an academic appointment (~1960–1989), before joining Suzuka University of Medical Science around 1989.

Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sophia University, Kyoto University, Cornell University (PhD) under Jay Jasanoff, and Osaka University (DLitt), later holding posts at Nagoya City Women's College and Nagoya City University.
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held an academic affiliation at Bukkyo University (attested in 2001 and 2013).

Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Koyasan University, where he subsequently served as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointed professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.
Kazumi Yoshizaki is a researcher in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Yoshizaki studied at Toyo University and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology (attested 2001).

Kazunobu Matsuda (born 1955) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Shiro Matsumoto. He lectured at Otani University (attested 1985–1989) and served as a professor at Bukkyo University from 1994.

Kazuo Hyodo (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, earning a PhD, and served as an associate professor at Otani University (~1984–2014).

Kazuo Kano (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg (PhD), he held academic posts at Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Komazawa University.

Kazuo Matsumura (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After studying at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976), he held positions at Tenri University (~1987–1997) and Wako University (~1997).

Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, he served as a lecturer at the Institute for Zen Studies and as a professor at Komazawa University (1979–2006).

Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1964), he served as an associate professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).
Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tamagawa University and held an academic post at Rissho University.
